correctness.rationale: In nonzero relative-speed channels the four-state backward boundary problem is noncharacteristic at zero rate, yielding analytic coefficients by explicit integration. value.rationale: The natural finite circular encounter problem asks whether adding reorientation noise helps detection when persistent agents move at distinct speeds. The exact ratio 1/sqrt(5) separates opposite initial responses and the positive quadratic borderline resolves the transition; the large-rate bound establishes an interior optimum above threshold. This is a structurally motivated threshold for transport design, not a mere known-table substitution.
